spec.title: Nullable and one-array parameters in property checks (H2, first step): the conformance corpus's JBMC and auto --confirm runs agree with the JVM
spec.description: Property checks gained a wider domain for array parameters (step H2 of llm-dlc/loops/foundations-heap.md): --nullable a lets a be null and --may-alias a,b lets a and b be one array. Only the own checker takes such a domain (each such parameter a symbolic reference among null and the arrays it may be); --engine jbmc and --confirm refuse it, and --engine auto does not fall back to JBMC. Witnesses say it (b=the same array as a, a=null) and keep it through the interpreter, the shrinker and the JVM run. The conformance corpus (lib/tests/conformance.rs) gained six claims over widened domains for twoArrays, length and lengthOrMinusOne, whose outside-the-domain calls ([0];@0 and null) they now take; the own checker's run of the corpus passed inline. This job runs the corpus's ignored tests, which run every claim through JBMC, --engine auto and auto --confirm and hold each to the JVM.
spec.expected: exits 0: both ignored tests pass. The six widened claims are Unverifiable under --engine jbmc and auto --confirm (refused: JBMC would prove a narrower claim), and under --engine auto have the own checker's verdicts (Verified, or Violation with a witness the JVM refutes); every other claim as before.

resources.notes: the corpus has about 90 claims, each run by JBMC once or more; earlier runs of these tests were pipeline jobs of comparable size
